# im

```go
import "github.com/lucasavila00/immutago/pkg/im"
```

Package im provides frozen data and local read projections checked by immutago.

Choose the API for the data:

- Copied: record fields that are copied with the value.
- Frozen: immutable fields that callers can store and share.
- Local: fields that follow the checker's local storage and transport rules.
- Cell: publish a snapshot and read the current value through a Projection.
- Projection: read selected data without a copy of its backing storage.
- FrozenSlice and FrozenMap: freeze a native collection without copying entries. Use Clone for an independent mutable copy.

Prepare a native collection in one local variable. After Freeze, use only the frozen value. Run immutago to enforce these rules; go build alone does not.


IsNil reports whether a pointer projection contains nil without exposing the pointer.

## func Unwrap

```go
func Unwrap[T any](value UncheckedValue[T]) *T
```

Unwrap returns the wrapped pointer, or nil for the zero UncheckedValue. Only the package that declares T can use Unwrap. Its API controls access to T.

## func Value

```go
func Value[T any](value Projection[T]) T
```

Value returns the value from a projection. The checker requires a Frozen read result: a Copied value, an opaque handle, a pointer to a Frozen handle wrapper, or an unnamed array of these values. Value does not allocate.

## type Cell

Cell stores a replaceable Frozen value. Its zero value has no stored value. Loads and Store are atomic. Readers can keep an earlier selected version. The checker proves T and restricts use of the returned local projections. A Cell must not be copied after first use. See https://github.com/lucasavila00/immutago/blob/main/docs/reference/cell.md for the complete forms.

```go
type Cell[T any] struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

### func \(\*Cell\[T\]\) Load

```go
func (c *Cell[T]) Load() Projection[T]
```

Load returns a local projection of the current value, or the zero T if no value was stored. It copies T by value without copying backing storage or allocating.

### func \(\*Cell\[T\]\) LoadPointer

```go
func (c *Cell[T]) LoadPointer() Projection[*T]
```

LoadPointer returns a local pointer projection without copying T or allocating. It returns a nil pointer projection before Store. The checker requires a Frozen record T.

### func \(\*Cell\[T\]\) Store

```go
func (c *Cell[T]) Store(value T)
```

Store publishes a private copy of value. A nonzero\-sized T needs one allocation. It copies T by value; it does not copy the immutable storage that T refers to.

## type Copied

Copied marks a record with bool, numeric, array, or Copied fields. Copying the record copies all its data. Strings and reference fields are rejected. Embed the marker by value. Ordinary copies use normal Go mutation and pointer rules. A field inside protected storage keeps its owner's write and address rules. See https://github.com/lucasavila00/immutago/blob/main/docs/reference/copied.md for the complete forms.

```go
type Copied struct{}
```

## type Frozen

Frozen marks a struct with immutable fields. Values and pointers to that struct can be copied, stored, and returned through the allowed source forms. Embed it by value. A named field or pointer embedding does not mark the struct. Only the marker can be embedded; all data fields must have names. See https://github.com/lucasavila00/immutago/blob/main/docs/reference/frozen-records.md for the complete forms.

```go
type Frozen struct{}
```

## type FrozenInterface

FrozenInterface marks an interface implemented by proved Frozen records. Embed it in a named interface. Each conversion needs an immutability proof; the private method alone does not prove the fields of an implementation. Methods have ordinary Go input and result contracts. Generated local projections forward these methods. Method implementations keep ordinary Go contracts, including retention of their own Frozen receiver. See https://github.com/lucasavila00/immutago/blob/main/docs/reference/frozen-interfaces.md for the complete forms.

```go
type FrozenInterface interface {
    // contains filtered or unexported methods
}
```

## type FrozenMap

FrozenMap is a read\-only map. Its zero value is empty. K and V must be Frozen types. Copies share the same read\-only entries.

```go
type FrozenMap[K comparable, V any] struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

### func FreezeMap

```go
func FreezeMap[K comparable, V any](values map[K]V) FrozenMap[K, V]
```

FreezeMap makes values read\-only without copying entries or allocating. Keep values in one local variable before Freeze. Afterward, read through the returned FrozenMap. The checker rejects aliases and use of the old map. Run immutago to enforce these rules; Freeze performs no runtime validation.

### func \(FrozenMap\[K, V\]\) All

```go
func (m FrozenMap[K, V]) All() iter.Seq2[K, V]
```

All returns an iterator over key\-value pairs in unspecified order. It reads frozen storage directly without making a copy. Each invocation starts a new map traversal and stops as soon as yield returns false.

### func \(FrozenMap\[K, V\]\) Clone

```go
func (m FrozenMap[K, V]) Clone() map[K]V
```

Clone returns an independent native map in O\(n\) time and space. It copies keys and values by value and preserves nil. Replacing entries in the copy does not change the frozen map. Pointers still point to the same Frozen objects. Opaque handles keep the same targets, which can be mutable.

### func \(FrozenMap\[K, V\]\) Get

```go
func (m FrozenMap[K, V]) Get(key K) (V, bool)
```

Get returns the value for key and whether it exists, using native map lookup. It allocates no storage and preserves Go's key equality rules.

### func \(FrozenMap\[K, V\]\) Len

```go
func (m FrozenMap[K, V]) Len() int
```

Len returns the number of entries in O\(1\) time without allocations.

### func \(FrozenMap\[K, V\]\) Projection

```go

```

Projection returns local read access without copying backing storage or allocating.

## type Projection

Projection holds a value for local reads. Its zero value contains the zero T. The checker proves T and restricts storage and transport of the projection. Copies copy T by value and share its immutable backing storage. See the complete forms at https://github.com/lucasavila00/immutago/blob/main/docs/reference/projection-primitives.md.

```go
type Projection[T any] struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

### func CopyRecord

```go
func CopyRecord[T any](value Projection[T]) Projection[*T]
```

CopyRecord allocates a private root copy and returns a local pointer projection. It copies T by value and shares immutable backing storage. A nonzero\-sized T needs one allocation. The checker requires a Frozen record T.

### func ProjectionOf

```go
func ProjectionOf[T any](value T) Projection[T]
```

ProjectionOf returns a local projection of value. It copies T by value without copying backing storage or allocating. Run immutago to enforce the local projection rules.

### func \(Projection\[T\]\) Unsafe

```go
func (p Projection[T]) Unsafe() T
```

Unsafe returns the selected Frozen value for use outside the local projection. It copies T by value without copying backing storage or allocating. A pointer result is the same pointer. The caller controls retention and must not change its target through reflection, unsafe code, or another API.

## type UncheckedValue

UncheckedValue holds an opaque pointer whose access rules belong to its declaring package. The target can be mutable. The checker does not prove its state or synchronization. UncheckedValue is Frozen and a read result, but not Copied. Any package can store, copy, pass, and return the handle. Only the package that declares T can use Trust and Unwrap. See https://github.com/lucasavila00/immutago/blob/main/docs/reference/unchecked-values.md for the complete forms.

```go
type UncheckedValue[T any] struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

### func Trust

```go
func Trust[T any](value *T) UncheckedValue[T]
```

Trust stores value without copying its target or adding synchronization. Only the package that declares T can use Trust.
